== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' is recorded as born or baptised on 18 February 1616 in Mid Calder, Midlothian, with James Glasgow and Agnes Adamson attached as his parents. The older profile cited only “Old Parish Records” for this event; the original entry and the precise birth/baptism distinction remain to be checked. The supplied NRS index names James Glasgow as father (Mid Calder OPR 694/10/28), supporting a confident father relationship for this record-defined child; the later adult-identity comparisons remain provisional.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Old Parish Registers, Mid Calder, John Glasgow, 18 February 1616, father James Glasgow, parish 694, reference 10/28; supplied Scotland’s People index, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ repository].</ref>

A John Glasgow and [[Patoune-11|Helen Patoune]] were named as parents of [[Glasgow-3014|John Glasgow]], recorded on 11 January 1638 at Duddingston, Midlothian.<ref>Duddingston Old Parish Register, parish 684, reference FR38, “JOHNE GLASGOW/HELENE PATOUNE,” entry for Johne, 11 January 1638; citation carried from the former Glasgow-3015 profile. The original page has not been compared with this index wording.</ref>

An index for [[Glasgow-1438|Issobell Glasgow]], recorded on 4 April 1643 at Edinburgh, names John Glasgow and [[Porteous-912|Issobell Porteous]] as parents.<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YN-JHD entry for Issobell Glasgow, 1643], naming John Glasgow and Issobell Porteous; cited on the child's profile.</ref> The 20 June 1652 Kirknewton and East Calder baptism of [[Glasgow-1439|Annah Glasgow]] names Johne Glasgow at Easter Newtoun but no mother.<ref name="EasterNewton2026" /> Its adult father is strongly supported as the man represented by [[Glasgow-3610|John Glasgow-3610]]. Identifying that adult with the 1616 child represented here, and attributing Porteous as the 1652 mother, remain unproved. The [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/4XPK-FW2 FamilySearch tree] is a family comparison rather than independent evidence of maternity.

[[Glasgow-3107|James Glasgow]] is also attached as a son. His own profile documents a 1663 marriage at Polwarth but says his parentage remains unconfirmed; that attachment must not be read as an established child of this John.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current Easter Newtoun working ancestry ===

The recorded father James-991 remains 98%; the possible adult identity, 42%, now supplies the preferred possible ancestry route for John-3610 at 40%.

The 40% is a combined judgement about James’s fatherhood of the later adult, not the 98% record-defined fatherhood of the 1616 child. The existing 42% childhood-to-adult comparison remains a distinct scoped assessment; these values are not independent measurements and are not mechanically multiplied. Both childhood dates fit an adult father in 1649: about 33 if baptised near birth in 1616, about 41 if in 1608. Neither childhood transcript supplies a residence, occupation or mother. The retained published Edinburgh marriage entry calls the 1642 groom a whipman but supplies no parents or residence to distinguish the candidates. The 1643 child names John and Issobell Porteous; the 1652 Annah transcript names no mother. A household, property, occupation or witness bridge to either childhood is still missing. Another local John, including the retained Linlithgow comparisons, or an unrepresented family remains possible. Robert-4006 remains a father-generation alternative. William-1087 remains a removed unsupported father, not biologically excluded merely by a 1609 baptism. John-1084 and John-3610 may be duplicate accounts, not two proved distinct sons named John; no merge is performed. Mothers remain separately assessed.

This reassessment reuses held evidence; it adds no newly inspected source. The retained Findmypast 1616 transcript reads “10 ?1616”, OPR 694/1 item 3 p.13; the supplied ScotlandsPeople index gives 18 February 1616, OPR 694/10/28. Preserve that discrepancy pending original comparison. The 1608 transcript gives 26 June, OPR 694/1 item 3 p.5. The 1649/1652 Findmypast pages, inspected on 18 October, give OPR 689/20 item 1 pp.5 and 13; supplied ScotlandsPeople references are 690/10/14 and 690/10/32. No original register was newly inspected. Repeated indexes of an event are not independent witnesses.

Prioritise a discriminating household link for the Easter Newtoun adult: compare original 1649/1652 entries and their neighbours, then any 1642 marriage details, kirk-session, land or inheritance evidence tying him to James’s Mid Calder family. Test the 1608/Quothquan route in parallel. A mother or a precise holding would be more useful than another generic name match.<ref name="EasterNewtonOrigin2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4585960&tab=this Findmypast, John, Mid Calder baptism, retained 1616 transcript; father James, OPR 694/1 item 3 p.13; date differs from supplied ScotlandsPeople index]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4585634&tab=this Findmypast, Jhone, Mid Calder, 26 June 1608; father Jhone, OPR 694/1 item 3 p.5; retained transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473470 Findmypast, John, 22 April 1649, father Johne at Easter Newtoune; transcript inspected 18 October 2026]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473604 Findmypast, Annah, 20 June 1652, father Johne at Easter Newtoun; transcript inspected 18 October 2026]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf Paton, Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh 1595–1700, printed p.267: John Glasgow, whipman, and Isobel Porteous, 30 June 1642; retained extract, no new page inspection]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YN-JHD FamilySearch, Isobell, Edinburgh, 4 April 1643; parents John Glasgow and Issobell Porteous; retained citation].</ref>

Earlier research below is retained as the history of the investigation. Where it calls John-3296 the selected father, or says the 28% ancestry is unchanged, that wording is superseded by the current James-991 selection at 40%. Other record roles and family grades are unchanged.


=== Easter Newtoun household ===

The following family reconstruction is superseded in its unqualified 1652 maternity and source assessment: ''Later entries name a John Glasgow with [[Porteous-912|Issobell Porteous]] as parents of [[Glasgow-1438|Issobell Glasgow]], recorded on 4 April 1643 in Edinburgh parish,<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YN-JHD entry for Issobell Glasgow, 1643], naming John Glasgow and Issobell Porteous; cited on the child's profile.</ref> and [[Glasgow-1439|Anne Glasgow]], recorded on 20 June 1652 at Kirknewton and East Calder. The latter child's profile cites a [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/4XPK-FW2 FamilySearch tree] rather than an inspected register entry, so its details remain to be verified.'' The inspected 1652 transcript now supplies a father and residence, while leaving the mother blank.

Prefer John [[Glasgow-3610]], the adult father in the 1649 Kirknewton baptism, as Annah [[Glasgow-1439]]’s father at 96% subjective confidence. Findmypast’s transcript of John’s 22 April 1649 baptism names father Johne Glasgow and residence Easter Newtoune. Its transcript of Annah’s 20 June 1652 baptism names father Johne Glasgow and residence Easter Newtoun. The matching uncommon full paternal name, specific residence, parish and three-year interval strongly support one household. This is a combined identity inference across two child records, not a literal statement that the children were siblings. A different Johne in the same settlement or a transcription error remains possible.

The 96% concerns the record-defined father of the 1652 child and his identification with the adult father of the 1649 child. It does not identify that adult with the John baptised at Mid Calder in 1616, prove his own father, or establish Annah’s later identity as the 1676 bride. The transcripts name no mother. Issobell Porteous’s existing maternal attachment remains separately unproved; no maternity is transferred to other children. The earlier [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow]] account may represent the same adult, but its 1616-child-to-adult identity remains possible at 42%, rather than established. These are overlapping profile-identity propositions, not mutually exclusive biological fathers; the percentages must not be added or treated as independent evidence. Retain that account as an alternative and resolve the possible duplicate before any live family change. No profiles are merged.

The Findmypast transcript pages were inspected on 18 October 2026; the parish originals were not inspected. The provider gives archive OPR 689/20, item 1, pages 5 and 13, while the supplied ScotlandsPeople index gives parish 690, references 10/14 and 10/32. Preserve that reference discrepancy for original comparison. Both Findmypast pages label the place Kirknewton and East Calder. The extra indexed version of Annah’s baptism, R_686208660, also names Johne and leaves the mother blank; it is another derivative of the same event, not independent corroboration. The September daily-limit responses are historical access failures; these targeted transcript retries now succeeded, without completing the wider Findmypast audit.

This is one proposed confident father-profile replacement, not a newly discovered biological father, a new birth event, a new connected branch or an upgrade of [[Glasgow-3610|John Glasgow]]’s own 28% father hypothesis. His earlier 1608-child comparison, [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow]] father, the conditional 1616-child/[[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]] alternative and all other ancestry grades remain unchanged. [[Glasgow-3012|John Glasgow]]’s existing 98% father role remains unchanged. All birth and death fields, mothers and saved WikiTree family fields are preserved. [[Glasgow-3112|Margaret Glasgow]]’s competing 1646/1649 readings are unresolved: her 26 November 1649 Findmypast transcript names John and Kirknewton/East Calder, but gives no residence. It does not independently place her in the Easter Newtoun household.

Compare the original 1649 and 1652 entries, their register references and neighbouring households; look for a recorded mother, occupation or witness tying the Easter Newtoun adult to the 1642 Porteous marriage and 1616 baptism. Shared residence alone does not choose his grandparents.<ref name="EasterNewton2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473470 Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, John, 22 April 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, provider OPR 689/20 item 1 p.5; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, original uninspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473604 Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, Annah, 20 June 1652, Kirknewton and East Calder, provider OPR 689/20 item 1 p.13; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, original uninspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473472 Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, Margaret, 26 November 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, provider OPR 689/20 item 1 p.5; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, original uninspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_686208660 Findmypast, Annah, 20 June 1652, R_686208660; additional index version, mother blank; inspected 18 October 2026].</ref>


The former Glasgow-3015 profile and this profile were combined as the leading identification. The 1638 Duddingston father and the father of the 1643 and 1652 children share a name, generation and neighbouring Midlothian parishes; there is no recorded overlap in the two maternal child sequences. No death of Helen Patoune, marriage to Issobell Porteous or continuous identifier has yet been found, so identifying both fathers as one man and inferring a second union remain provisional. The earlier profile's approximate 1618 birth was an adult-status estimate, not a separate birth record.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow in Rashlie, Kilbride, 1643. John Glasgow was listed as “in Rashlie, parish of Kilbride” in a printed index to Glasgow Commissary Court testaments, dated 17 April 1643.<ref>FamilySearch, ''Glasgow. Wills 1547–1800'', item #007960708, image 112, printed index p. 196, entry for John Glasgow in Rashlie, parish of Kilbride, 17 April 1643, reference CC9/7/28; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS8K-D98V?view=fullText&keywords=Glasgow&searchForm=advanced&lang=en&groupId=M97N-2NT. The image is of the printed index, not the underlying testament.</ref> The identification remains uncertain.
